assessment.rationale: Inner speech decoding works in a handful of implanted participants and nowhere else, so the Main KPI of 8,000,000,000 people able to use speech decoding is open work. The strongest result is Kunz et al. (Cell 2025): in four participants with intracortical motor-cortex arrays, inner speech is robustly represented, imagined sentences were decoded in real time, and a separable motor-intent dimension plus deliberate safeguards were needed to stop a speech neuroprosthesis decoding private inner speech (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=%22inner%20speech%22%20AND%20%22intracortical%22%20AND%20neuroprosthesis&format=json&pageSize=5&resultType=core). Non-invasive decoding does not generalise: EEG inner-speech studies report 90 to 98 percent within-subject accuracy on datasets of 5 to 10 participants but only 52 to 64 percent cross-subject, and a functional-connectivity study of 10 participants on four Spanish words reached 43.7 percent. A 2026 systematic review puts invasive median multiclass accuracy at 77.7 percent and notes only six studies validated results in paralysed people, all invasive. Open source is hobby-scale: 15 repositories, the largest with 6 stars (https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=speech+decoding+brain+computer+interface&per_page=10&sort=stars). Honest limits: intracortical inner-speech decoding is published prior art, so replicating it is a known answer; the open work is non-invasive, cross-subject, open-vocabulary decoding, and the consent and privacy machinery a universal KPI would demand, which the Cell paper raises but does not solve.

additionalSearches.finding: Kunz et al., Cell 2025 (PMID 40816265): four participants with intracortical motor-cortex recordings; inner speech is robustly represented and imagined sentences were decoded in real time, with a motor-intent dimension separating inner from attempted speech and explicit strategies to avoid decoding private inner speech. No vocabulary size or accuracy in the abstract.

additionalSearches.query: EEG and non-invasive inner speech decoding accuracy
additionalSearches.finding: EEG inner-speech studies report high within-subject accuracy on small datasets (about 95-96 percent on 5 participants, 90.23 percent on 10, 98.81 percent on a four-class dataset) but cross-subject accuracy of only 64.09 and 52.19 percent; a functional-connectivity study of 10 participants imagining four words reached 43.7 percent. A 2026 systematic review gives median 77.7 percent multiclass accuracy for invasive approaches, with only six studies validated in paralysed people, all invasive.

additionalSearches.query: open-source speech and inner-speech BCI code
additionalSearches.finding: 15 repositories, the largest with 6 stars: EEG imagined-speech models on the Chisco dataset, consumer 8-channel headband inner-speech demos, a Kaggle brain-to-text entry, and small frameworks. No open system approaches usable inner-speech decoding at scale.

additionalSearches.query: assistive deployment of decoding and description systems for daily use
additionalSearches.finding: Checked as a comparison for what population-scale assistive deployment looks like: wearable assistive systems reach real users (a 2026 JVIB survey of 254 workers found 10.2 percent wearable use, nearly all smart glasses), whereas no comparable deployment exists for speech decoding, which remains confined to research participants.
